Problem 761. Following water from Silver River
River systems form directed networks: water has a direction, tributaries join larger streams, and upstream/downstream are relational concepts.

Silver River flows into Blue Creek; Clearwater flows into Blue Creek; Blue Creek flows into Meadow River. A canal diverts some water from Clearwater to a reservoir, but the remaining flow still reaches Blue Creek.
If river X flows into river Y, X is upstream of Y. Upstream relations can be followed through several confluences. Downstream is the reverse direction of flow.
Is Silver River upstream of Meadow River? Can water from Silver River reach Meadow River through the stated network?

1. Rewrite the facts as arrows: Silver River→Blue Creek, Clearwater→Blue Creek, Blue Creek→Meadow River. 2. Follow arrows starting from Silver River. 3. An arrow path reaches Meadow River, so Silver River is upstream of Meadow River.
Yes; water from Silver River can reach Meadow River.
A river network can be reasoned about like any directed network; following the arrows is more reliable than guessing from names.
Directed graph; edge X→Y means water can flow from X to Y; query reachability.
